visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 more consistently represents the shaded regions as concentric annuli with the correct alternating pattern and final 64-circle interpretation, while Lesson 1 has misleading non-concentric/tangent circle diagrams and a bite-shaped subtraction visual that do not accurately match the annular nested-circle concept.

interactivity.rationale: Both lessons have absent gate specs and absent plan JSON, so neither shows any functional checkpoints or input-accepting questions.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 2 provides clear, natural narration with spoken math rendered appropriately and no obvious TTS defects, while Lesson 1 has no transcript at all, making its narration absent and therefore worse on this dimension.

sync.rationale: Lesson 2 at least provides a narration sequence that suggests when visuals should appear, whereas Lesson 1 has no transcript or timing data at all, making its sync impossible to verify and therefore worse.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 reaches the correct formula and answer and mostly explains the alternating-area sum clearly, despite incorrectly describing the circles as concentric/common-center rather than sharing a common point, whereas Lesson 1 has no available transcript or content to verify any correct conceptual teaching.

polish.rationale: Lesson 2 has a much more polished, legible, consistently styled notebook layout with large centered text and clean visuals, while Lesson 1 often uses tiny left-side text, sparse off-center compositions, inconsistent color emphasis, and even a partially drawn/awkward visual at the summary stage.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 2 is the clear overall winner: five of the six dimensions favor it, many with high confidence. It is judged stronger in visual accuracy, narration quality, sync, concept accuracy, and polish. The only non-Lesson-2 result is interactivity, which is a high-confidence tie because neither lesson includes functional checkpoints or input-based interaction. Lesson 2’s main weakness is a conceptual/visual imprecision about the circles being concentric/common-center rather than sharing a common point, but it still reaches the correct formula and answer and is substantially more complete, legible, and polished than Lesson 1, which lacks transcript/content evidence and has weaker visuals.
